Last Friday (the 21st), the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China case was handed down. In the early hours, police escorted a woman who had been queuing to attend the hearing onto a police vehicle. In response to enquiries, the police stated that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "sedition".

In the early hours of last Friday (around 5 a.m.), more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During that time, a plainclothes police officer pointed out that a woman in the queue was "suspected of wearing a T-shirt with somewhat seditious intent", and escorted her onto a police vehicle. While the officers took the woman away, several officers repeatedly directed journalists to leave, saying "I'll take you to the press area", and pulled an orange cordon line out towards Ying Wa Street. Once the woman had boarded the police vehicle, the cordon was taken down. A "court-watching volunteer" who was queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective (集誌社) enquired with the police about why the woman had been taken away and whether she had been arrested. The police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Courts on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place", "resisting or willfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty", and "sedition", and was being detained for investigation.
